name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Weird Machine Compositors: Exploiting AI Orchestration at the Expression Layer
items.dek: Expression-layer sandbox escapes in n8n orchestration platform via weird machine exploitation; three CVEs (CVSS 9.4), AST coverage tool released, pattern generalizes across category.

items.title: CVE-2026-86950 — Apple Multiple Products Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability
items.dek: Apple Multiple Products. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 2 October.

items.title: Tracekit: Tamper-Evident Intent-Reasoning-Action Auditing for Autonomous Coding Agents
items.dek: Hash-chained ledger system for coding agents detects all mutations; detects tampering under concurrent writes and long retention.
items.unproven: whether agents will actually accept pre-execution policy gates in production; adoption by major platforms untested.

items.title: "Nothing to See Here'': Unintended Disclosure through Revision Traces of LLM Deliverables
items.dek: LLM edit comments leak 8.8% of deleted secrets; affects drafting workflows in regulated environments.
items.unproven: limited to three public corpora; real-world leak rates in production agents unknown

items.title: Trajectory-Level Security Debt in LLM Coding Agents
items.dek: Security Debt Line Integral metric shows SAST tool agreement in agent code trajectories is 3.9% to 6.2%, not final-state artifacts alone.
items.unproven: evaluation uses four SAST tools and three code-generation benchmarks; unclear how scanner agreement translates to validated vulnerabilities in production agents

items.title: Breaking Windows Malware Detection: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Problem-Space Adversarial Robustness
items.dek: Large-scale evaluation of nine evasion attacks on eight Windows malware detectors shows raw-byte models vulnerable to problem-space manipulation; no detector uniformly robust.
items.unproven: Study is Windows-focused; applicability to Linux/macOS malware detectors and detector tuning recommendations for the reader's environment not provided.

items.title: The Privacy Fallacy of Crowdsourced Fine-Tuning: Extracting Proprietary Data via Topic-Based Poisoning
items.dek: Malicious crowdsourced fine-tuning data poisons LLM SFT pipelines to extract 3–4× more training data; directly applicable to model governance in SDLC.
items.unproven: attack demonstrated on public models and datasets; generalization to proprietary training pipelines with other filtering or isolation controls unclear

items.title: The Price of Peeking: Anytime-Valid Leakage Detection on ML-KEM EM Traces
items.dek: Anytime-valid leakage detection via betting on ML-KEM EM traces; reduces required sample count 2–8% of fixed budget while controlling false-alarm rate uniformly over time.
items.unproven: Generalization to post-quantum algorithms other than ML-KEM; cost-benefit analysis of repeated monitoring versus fixed-horizon testing in production labs.

items.title: HESP: Separating What to Probe from When to Stop in Local LLM Alert-Triage Agents
items.dek: HESP controller separates investigation procedure from small local LLM agents using ledger, expected-information-gain probe selection, and evidence-backed verdicts; lifts completion from 0.125 to 1.0 on 7B model.
items.unproven: Generalization beyond controlled lab environment; performance with real multi-stage alert chains; scaling to enterprise alert volumes.

items.title: API Secrets Should Never Become Tokens in the LLM's Vocabulary: A Threat Analysis of API Credential Handling in LLM Agent Systems and an Empirical Evaluation of a Vault-Mediated Execution Boundary
items.dek: Vault-mediated execution boundary prevents LLM agent credential exposure across conversation history, logs, and error payloads; Corvic evaluation shows authenticated API calls succeed without plaintext secrets in environment.
items.unproven: Applicability to non-GitHub APIs and custom tool connectors; usability overhead in production agent workflows; side-channel leakage in logs or monitoring.

items.title: When Cyber Scoring Systems Diverge: An Empirical Comparison
items.dek: CVSS, EPSS, SSVC, and IronMiner diverge significantly on Ukraine 2015 power grid topology; scoring choice drives mitigation strategy.
items.unproven: single historical incident; does not establish which scorer is more reliable for current vulnerability triage

items.title: Practical Secrets Extraction against Black-box LLMs
items.dek: Black-box extraction of secrets from LLMs via distillation and top-p sampling without weight access.
items.unproven: Controlled API-key benchmarks only; real-world evaluation explicitly stated as limited; no systematic measurement of data retention in major coding agents.

items.title: CyberPersistBench: Evaluating LLM-Based Cyber Attackers on Installation and Persistence
items.dek: First benchmark for LLM persistence post-compromise shows frontier agents maintain footholds only 27–44% of the time across system disruptions.
items.unproven: Measures agent behavior in lab environments with sandbox host mechanisms; does not establish whether results transfer to defended enterprise infrastructure or inform defensive posture for agents in SDLC.

items.title: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents
items.dek: SEABench benchmark shows self-evolving agents increase safety failures even without adversarial input; spans 48 task sequences.
items.unproven: whether failures persist outside simulated environments; generalization across agent architectures beyond those tested.

items.title: Share-Borne AI Virus: Memory-Hopping Attacks Across LLM Agents
items.dek: Artifacts shared between independent agents enable propagation of adversarial prompts across eight hops and 60-80% of simulated agents.
items.unproven: real-world propagation in production systems; whether current agent isolation mechanisms block the attack in practice.

items.title: When Valid Tool Calls Change Meaning: Formation-Consistent Dispatch for LLM Agents
items.dek: Formation-consistent dispatch prevents tool-call meaning drift when implementation changes during rollout or reconnection in LLM agents.
items.unproven: four profiles and stock releases tested; applicability depends on whether reader's agents use third-party tool implementations subject to version skew

items.title: Physics-Attested Federated Learning: Securing Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Critical Water Infrastructure
items.dek: Cyber-physical invariants mined from clean water-system telemetry reject all fabricated federated-learning updates and 12–20 of 35 real attacks on SWaT and WADI testbeds.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to two water-system testbeds; no evidence invariant mining scales to other OT domains or that honest-shard rejection rate remains zero under adaptive poisoning by attackers with knowledge of the invariants.

items.title: SEAD: A State-Based Perspective on Attack and Defense in Tool-Using Agents
items.dek: State-based framework formalizes attack and defense in tool-using agents; DART and SAGE demonstrate 19–36pp improvement in attack success and blocking accuracy.
items.unproven: Evaluation on four models only; transferability to production agent architectures and tool compositions outside the experimental set not established.

items.title: CoDeL: Co-Evolutionary Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM-based Agents
items.dek: CoDeL co-evolves defender and attacker to harden agents against deferred indirect prompt injection across multi-turn workflows using decoupled reward optimization.
items.unproven: Evaluation on one agent architecture; effectiveness against real-world agent deployments and out-of-distribution attack strategies not demonstrated.

items.title: ReproBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Reproducing Vulnerability From Scratch
items.dek: ReproBench evaluates LLM agents on end-to-end CVE reproduction from identifier alone, decomposing six phases with verifiable artifacts across 30 IoT firmware vulnerabilities.
items.unproven: IoT firmware focus; generalizability to enterprise application vulnerabilities and agent performance on non-firmware exploitation workflows unclear.

items.title: Certified Multi-Source Integrity for Structured Agent Actions
items.dek: Certifier for structured agent actions bounds corruption across multi-source evidence using hitting sets and deterministic reconciliation; validation on 70,966 sanctions records.
items.unproven: Evaluation on sanctions designations only; applicability to financial transaction fields, invoice payment, and real-world agent action spaces not demonstrated.

items.title: LoRo-Mark:Provably Lossless and Robust Agent Watermarking
items.dek: LoRo-Mark watermarks LLM agents to detect repackaging via black-box forensic branch; directly relevant as agents enter SDLC.
items.unproven: robustness tested only against partial execution modification, not full adversarial model theft; production deployment not demonstrated

items.title: Near-Duplicate Families Break Exact-Record Membership Inference
items.dek: Near-duplicate families cause membership inference auditors to mislabel 99.7% of non-members as members; four-world audit separates exact inclusion from family presence.
items.unproven: whether downstream model owners or auditors will adopt the four-world methodology; cost and scale of applying it to production datasets.

items.title: Where the Numbers Come From: Auditing Evaluation in Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection
items.dek: Audit of nine provenance-based intrusion detectors isolates three measurement artifacts that inflate reported precision by 0.16–0.33 without changing detector rank.
items.unproven: Prevalence of these defects in detectors not examined; whether corrected implementations change architectural decisions.

items.title: Leaky Students: Membership Inference against On-Policy Distillation
items.dek: Membership inference attacks on distilled language models extract sensitive training data via token log-probability gaps on fresh trajectories.
items.unproven: Scaling to production model sizes; transferability to defenses like differential privacy; practical threshold selection for deployment.

noise.title: Armada: Encrypted, Open-Source, Discord Alternative (Built on Nostr)
noise.dek: Armada offers encrypted messaging on Nostr protocol as Discord alternative.
noise.unproven: not relevant to reader's SDLC, tooling, or architecture governance; commercial product

noise.title: Who wrote Elizabeth I's most scathing letters?
noise.dek: Historical analysis of Elizabeth I's letter authorship using linguistic methods.

noise.title: First Steps of the PLC Organization – Independent Public Ledger of Credentials
noise.dek: PLC Organization proposes a public ledger for credential management and verification.
noise.unproven: production adoption, interoperability with existing identity systems, resistance to credential harvesting at scale
